```suggestion
enum class PlayerID : uint8_t {
```
Proper form, all other cases with `ID` is this form

I think these new parameters should be bit flags instead of individual player IDs. That (1) allows the caller the flexibility to check multiple players at once and (2) enables us to maintain backwards compatibility. Regarding (2), these current methods will consider *all* devices, and it's reasonable to expect these to consider *all* players by default.

This definitely works, but I'm wondering if we could instead have a project setting `input/joy_player_id_override` that's a `Dictionary` type which maps device ID to player ID. That way developers can define all of the mappings statically ahead of time or just use the existing `ProjectSettings` API to programmatically change at runtime.

Does that offer any benefit over implementing this on the `Input` singleton?

Is this something that Godot users *need* to call in order for `player` to be properly set or does the engine call this as needed? I think it's the latter, but I saw some documentation for this method below so I'm unclear if it's intended to be public and, if so, when a Godot user is expected to call this.
You are probably right. Should we wait for some other mantainer feedback or do you feel this is safe to change?
Yeah, it's only internal. I was probably unsure when I implemented this.

Ahead of time stuff seems good. How would that look to be backward compatible?
Something like (?):
Device 0 : Player 0
Device 1 : Player 1
Because I'm not sure...

The `ProjectSettings` API is also a good idea, but I'm wondering if this detaches too much the player ID management from the device...
We can wait for additional feedback! I don't want you to have to do extra work that ends up being not needed.

body: This method is too specific and should not be exposed in my opinion. From what I am understanding of this PR, this can be accomplished by assigning the result of Input's `get_joy_player_id` to the input event's `player`

We likely need to update [`_find_event`](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/7ed0b6167618f9c8c5df87c7e83da6003c081368/core/input/input_map.cpp#L144-L162) to support matching stored events (i.e. events stored for an action) with incoming player-specific events. Right now it doesn't handle the case where a developer defines an input event and wants it to match against *all* players by default (much like `ALL_DEVICES` is available for defining events that match against all device IDs). We could either create a similar sentinel value `ALL_PLAYERS` or actually store a bitflag with the default value having all player IDs toggled on (better IMO).

For more context, see the discussion in the Godot developer chat: https://chat.godotengine.org/channel/input?msg=NtexvJPXZoB4NGBe9.

> From what I understand, this PR does not touch the Input Map panel much. It's a missed opportunity though, as it means that different input events assigned to different players are hard to discern.

@Mickeon does this relate to your concern above? Much like how InputMap allows players to select which device IDs an input event belongs to when defining actions, we need to provide a mechanism for defining which players an event belongs to (so that we can handle per-player bindings).
